metadata.title: fix(api): support multipart/form-data and form-urlencoded for REST tool invocations
metadata.author: madhav165

description:
## 📌 Summary
REST tools always sent request bodies as `application/json` regardless of what the upstream API required. Any API expecting `multipart/form-data` or `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` would return 400 Bad Request with no way to configure the encoding.

## 🔁 Reproduction Steps
Closes #4058

1. Register a REST tool pointing to an API that requires `multipart/form-data` (e.g. uses `-F` form fields)
2. Set `Content-Type: multipart/form-data` in the tool's headers
3. Invoke the tool — previously returned 400 Bad Request

## 🐞 Root Cause
`tool_service.py` hardcoded `json=payload` for all non-GET REST requests, causing httpx to always serialize the body as JSON and override any user-configured `Content-Type` header with `application/json`.

## 💡 Fix Description
After all header modifications (auth merge, passthrough, plugin hooks, header mapping), inspect the final `Content-Type` header and dispatch to the appropriate httpx body encoding:

- `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` → `data=` (scalars stringified, nested values JSON-encoded)
- `multipart/form-data` → `files=` with `Content-Type` stripped so httpx sets the correct `boundary=` parameter
- Anything else (including unset or `application/json`) → `json=` — unchanged default, no behaviour change for existing tools

No DB/schema/migration changes — behaviour is driven entirely by the `Content-Type` header already stored on the tool.

## 🧪 Verification

| Check                             | Command                                                                                  | Status |
|-----------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------|
| Lint suite                        | `make lint`                                                                              | ✅     |
| Unit tests                        | `uv run pytest tests/unit/mcpgateway/services/test_tool_service.py -v`                  | ✅ 337/337 |
| New encoding tests                | `uv run pytest tests/unit/mcpgateway/services/test_tool_service.py -k "rest_post" -v`   | ✅ 4/4  |
| Manual regression no longer fails | Register a REST tool with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded`, invoke it — response `form` field contains parameters instead of 400 | ✅ |

## 📐 MCP Compliance (if relevant)
- [x] Matches current MCP spec
- [x] No breaking change to MCP clients

## ✅ Checklist
- [x] Code formatted (`make black isort pre-commit`)
- [x] No secrets/credentials committed

reviews.author: marekdano
reviews.body:
@madhav165 - the PR looks good, just a few issues

#### Summary

  Fixes issue #4058 by detecting the final `Content-Type` header after all auth/plugin/mapping transformations and dispatching to the appropriate httpx encoding (`data=, files=, or json=`). The core fix is correct, backward-compatible, and the happy-path test coverage is solid.

####  Findings

- `mcpgateway/services/tool_service.py:4283` — Design: nested function definition
  `_to_str` is defined inside the method body, creating a new function object on every code-path execution. Extract it as a `@staticmethod _form_value_to_str(v: Any) -> str on ToolService`.

- `mcpgateway/services/tool_service.py:4295–4309` — Correctness: undocumented query param behavioral asymmetry
  The JSON/default path merges URL query params into the request body (`payload.update(query_params)`). The form-urlencoded and multipart paths forward them as `params=_qp` (query string). This is the more semantically correct behavior for form encoding, but it is a silent behavioral difference for any tool that switches content types. Add an inline comment explaining the intentional asymmetry.

- `mcpgateway/services/tool_service.py:4274` — Consistency: opaque variable name
  `_qp` is not self-explanatory. Rename to _url_query_params or inline the ternary directly at its two call sites.

- Test coverage: GET + form-related `Content-Type`
  No test guards against a GET request where `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` is set. The GET branch correctly wins in the dispatch, but there is no regression guard for this.

- Test coverage: `tool_query_mapping` + form-urlencoded
  No test verifies that when `tool_query_mapping` is set, `_qp` is `None` and the mapped payload is sent in the form body rather than forwarded as query string params.

reviews.author: marekdano
reviews.body:
The core fix is well-structured and the test coverage is solid. A few security-relevant items worth addressing before merge, ranging from a meaningful behavioral issue to lower-priority correctness gaps.

---

## Blocking

**`Content-Type` is not in the sensitive header blocklist, enabling encoding dispatch manipulation via `header_mapping`**

The new dispatch logic routes requests to `data=`, `files=`, or `json=` based on `_ct_base`, which is read from the **final, post-mapping** `headers` dict. Because `Content-Type` is not blocked by `_is_sensitive_tool_header_name()` (see `_SENSITIVE_TOOL_HEADER_PATTERNS` in `tool_service.py`), an admin can configure a tool with `header_mapping: { "encoding": "Content-Type" }`. A caller with only tool-invoke rights could then pass `{ "encoding": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" }` and silently switch the upstream request from JSON to form-encoded — or vice versa.

This may not be an issue in practice (it requires an admin to create a Content-Type mapping, which is an unusual configuration), but it creates a surprising attack surface: the encoding path becomes caller-controllable, which is almost certainly unintentional. Worth a targeted decision here:

**Option A (minimal):** Add `content-type` to `_SENSITIVE_TOOL_HEADER_PATTERNS` so `header_mapping` cannot target it.

**Option B (defense-in-depth):** Determine `_ct_base` from the tool's *statically configured* headers before mapping is applied, not after. This is a stronger guarantee but a larger change.

A deny-path test covering this scenario would be valuable regardless.

---

## Should Fix

**Boolean serialization in `_form_value_to_str` produces `"True"`/`"False"`, not `"true"`/`"false"`**

```python
return str(v)  # str(True) == "True"
```

For form APIs that inspect boolean flag fields (e.g., `admin=true`, `enabled=true`), this will silently fail with the capitalized variant. `orjson.dumps` already handles booleans correctly:

```python
if isinstance(v, (dict, list, bool)):
    return orjson.dumps(v).decode()  # produces "true" / "false"
```

There is currently no test asserting `_form_value_to_str(True)` behaviour.

---

**`_url_query_params` initialization doesn't account for `has_header_mapping`**

```python
_url_query_params = query_params if not tool_query_mapping else None
```

When `has_header_mapping=True` and `has_query_mapping=False`, the mapping block (lines 4685–4707) already strips and processes URL query params into `query_params`. The form branch then receives that processed dict as `params=` via `_url_query_params`, but the URL-stripping block below is skipped (guarded by `not has_header_mapping`). The result is that processed URL params could be forwarded as query string parameters on form-encoded requests — a subtle double-send. The initialization should mirror the extraction guard:

```python
_url_query_params = query_params if not tool_query_mapping and not tool_header_mapping else None
```

This case is also untested.

---

## Suggestions

Please feel free to fix the following in this PR or in a newly created one.

**`multipart/form-data`: all fields are sent as file attachments**

Using `files=` for every field sends `Content-Disposition: form-data; filename=""` on each part. For APIs that expect standard form fields alongside actual file uploads, this will break. The standard httpx pattern is `data=` for plain fields and `files=` only for file parts. For a v1 fix this is acceptable, but worth a comment and a known-limitations note so future contributors don't have to rediscover it.

**`parse_qs(..., v[0])` silently drops duplicate query parameters**

Both the existing code (lines 4688, 4720) and the new form path use `v[0]` to take only the first value of repeated keys. This is consistent, but for signed URLs (AWS presigned, Azure SAS) that sometimes include repeated params for multi-value filters, silent truncation could corrupt the signature. A logged warning here similar to the GET conflict warning (lines 4722–4728) would help debugging.

**No size guard on `orjson.dumps(v)` for nested values**

A caller could pass a deeply nested dict or very large list as a form field value, causing `orjson.dumps` to allocate significant memory before the request is sent. Existing payload size limits upstream may already cover this, but it is worth verifying — and if not, a max-depth or max-size check before serialization would be prudent.

reviews.author: marekdano
reviews.body:
## Summary

Adds `application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and `multipart/form-data` encoding support to REST tools, moving beyond hardcoded JSON. The implementation is correct, backward-compatible, and security-aware.

---

## Resolved Items

| Item | Status |
|------|--------|
| Boolean serialization (`true`/`false`) | ✅ Fixed — `bool` added to `isinstance` check in `_form_value_to_str`, now uses `orjson.dumps()` |
| Content-Type in sensitive header blocklist | ✅ Fixed — `content-type` added to `_SENSITIVE_TOOL_HEADER_PATTERNS` (Option A) |
| multipart `files={'field': (None, value)}` | ✅ Correct — httpx emits no `filename=` with `None`; proper form field behaviour |
| `parse_qs` `v[0]` dropping duplicates | ✅ Pre-existing pattern, out of scope |

---

## `_url_query_params` / `has_header_mapping` — Author Is Right

After tracing the logic, the author's explanation is accurate:

```
Scenario: has_header_mapping=True, has_query_mapping=False
1. Lines 4685–4688: URL stripped → query_params populated
2. Line 4711: _url_query_params = query_params  ✓  (tool_query_mapping is falsy)
3. Line 4718 extraction block: skipped (has_header_mapping=True)  ✓
4. Lines 4756/4763 form branches: params=_url_query_params  ✓
```

Adding `and not tool_header_mapping` to line 4711 **would be a regression** — it would set `_url_query_params = None` and silently drop URL params from form/multipart requests when only header mapping is configured. Header mapping is orthogonal to URL query param forwarding.

---

## Suggestions (Non-blocking)

1. **Add a comment at line 4711** to document the invariant and prevent future regression:
   ```python
   # NB: guard on tool_query_mapping, not has_header_mapping. When only
   # header_mapping is present, URL params were already extracted into
   # query_params above and must still be forwarded on the query string.
   ```

2. **Add one test** for `header_mapping`-only (no `query_mapping`) to lock in the subtle behaviour:
   ```python
   # URL has ?key=value, tool has header_mapping only
   # Assert final request has params={'key': 'value'} on query string
   ```

---

## Security

- **Content-Type blocking:** Effective — prevents encoding dispatch manipulation via `header_mapping`
- **`_form_value_to_str()`:** No injection vectors — all types serialized as strings, not interpreted
- **Signed URL preservation:** Correct — form paths forward URL params via `params=`, not merged into body

---

## Test Coverage

- ✅ Form-urlencoded POST with nested values
- ✅ Multipart form-data with various types
- ✅ Query parameter forwarding for both encodings
- ✅ Interaction with `query_mapping`
- ✅ Interaction with `header_mapping`
- ✅ Edge case: GET request with form Content-Type (correctly stays GET)

All blocking issues resolved, implementation correct and secure

LGTM 🚀

REST tools always sent request bodies as application/json regardless of
the upstream API's requirements. Detect the final Content-Type header
(after auth, plugin, and header-mapping modifications) and dispatch to
the appropriate httpx body encoding:

- application/x-www-form-urlencoded → data= (scalars stringified, nested JSON-encoded)
- multipart/form-data → files= with Content-Type stripped so httpx sets the boundary
- anything else → json= (existing default, no behaviour change)

Closes #4058

commits.message:
fix(api): preserve URL query params for form-encoded and multipart REST requests

The form-urlencoded and multipart/form-data branches did not forward
URL-embedded query parameters, silently dropping them. Pass query_params
via httpx params= so they remain on the query string instead of being
lost.

Also move an inline json import to the module top in the test file.

Closes #4058

commits.message:
fix(api): extract URL query params for form-encoded and multipart POST without mappings

When no query_mapping or header_mapping is configured, form-urlencoded and
multipart POST requests were not extracting query parameters from the tool
URL.  The params stayed as an empty dict and the query string remained
embedded in the URL, causing params= to be empty.

Strip the query string from the URL and populate params= so query
parameters are forwarded on the query string, matching the existing GET
behaviour.

Signed-off-by: Madhav Kandukuri <madhav165@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Brian Hussey <brian.hussey@ie.ibm.com>

commits.message:
refactor(api): address PR #4139 review feedback

- Extract nested _to_str as @staticmethod _form_value_to_str on ToolService
  to avoid re-creating a function object on every invocation.
- Rename opaque _qp variable to _url_query_params for clarity.
- Add inline comments documenting the intentional query-param behavioral
  asymmetry between form-encoded (params=) and JSON (payload merge) paths.
- Guard the new form/multipart URL query-param extraction with method != GET
  so GET requests with a form Content-Type still follow the GET branch.
- Add regression tests: GET with form Content-Type header, and
  form-urlencoded POST with query_mapping set.
